_note: The temporal arm. The camera tracks 4.4 m laterally in two seconds while holding its aim on the fence corridor, so every frame has a large, smooth, exactly-known screen motion and the fence slats pass in front of each other -- which is what the disocclusion mask exists to exclude. Linear interpolation on purpose: an eased dolly has a near-zero velocity at each end, and a residual measured where nothing moved is a measurement of the static case wearing a moving camera's name. Two seconds at 30 fps is 60 frames, enough for a residual to have a tail worth reporting and short enough to render twice -- candidate and supersampled reference -- inside one GPU lock.
_parametersNote: `post/output/antialias` is set EXPLICITLY and it is not a detail. It defaults to 0.0 in scene/post_settings.hpp -- '0 skips the pass entirely' -- so a scene that does not ask for FXAA never runs it, and `--disable fxaa` on such a scene produces a DIAGNOSTIC-render warning and a byte-identical sequence hash. That is ADR-182's exact failure shape: an attribution arm whose null result is indistinguishable from a broken instrument, and it happened here on the first attempt at ADR-243's three arms. An anti-aliasing benchmark has to have anti-aliasing switched on before it can be switched off. 0.75 is the value world/art_direction.hpp uses.
